---
title: Plugins
description: Every non-JAX component behind one interface, running wherever you point it.
---

A plugin is a non-JAX component (a mesher, a tet filler, a solver) reached
through `apply` and `vjp`, with declared inputs, outputs and differentiable
inputs. cadjoint asks the registry for a kind and does not know whether the
component runs in this process, in a container or behind a Kubernetes Service.

## Example

```python
from cadjoint.plugins import plugin_for_kind

solver = plugin_for_kind("thermal_solver")
print(solver.name, solver.version)             # thermal_jaxfem 0.1.0
print(sorted(solver.capabilities.differentiable_inputs))
# ['cell_conductivity', 'conductivity', 'points', 'source']
print(solver.capabilities.supports("per_element_properties"))   # True
print(solver.probe())
```

The Tesseract transports need the `tesseract` extra (`uv sync --extra tesseract`).

## Plugin attributes

Plugins are [Tesseracts](https://github.com/pasteurlabs/tesseract-core): typed
`apply` and `vector_jacobian_product` endpoints, lifted into a JAX primitive by
[tesseract-jax](https://github.com/pasteurlabs/tesseract-jax). tesseract-core
and tesseract-jax encode arrays, speak HTTP, declare schemas and implement the
autodiff primitive; `cadjoint.plugins` provides the kind vocabulary, the
registry, and the configuration that maps a name to one `Tesseract.from_*`
call.

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **name** | the registry key, e.g. `thermal_jaxfem` |
| **kind** | the slot it fills. cadjoint asks for the `PluginKind` values `mesher`, `tetfill`, `tet_mesher`, `thermal_solver`, `elastic_solver`, `flow_solver`, and the five [pluggable kinds](#pluggable-kinds). The field is a plain string, so a plugin may declare a kind cadjoint does not know |
| **version** | what the running instance advertises, else what its `tesseract_config.yaml` declares |
| **inputs / outputs** | the schema `tesseract-runtime` publishes, never restated in Python. For a `python` plugin, the annotations of its contract's `Protocol` |
| **capabilities** | derived from the schema: differentiable inputs and outputs, served endpoints, and named flags (`per_element_properties`, `body_force`, `frozen_topology`, `vjp`, …) |
| **apply / vjp** | the component's own endpoints |
| **as_jax()** | `tesseract_jax.apply_tesseract` bound to this plugin, the JAX primitive with its `custom_vjp`. For a `python` plugin, the object's own method |
| **probe()** | `/health`, the reported version, and a hash of the served schema |

Anything not defined on a plugin is forwarded to the `Tesseract`, so
`plugin.jacobian(...)`, `plugin.jacobian_vector_product(...)`,
`plugin.abstract_eval(...)` and `plugin.server_logs()` work without a wrapper.

## Shipped plugins

| Name | Kind | Wraps | Boundary crossed | VJP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mesher` | `mesher` | the whole mesher: lattice field → surface → volume | a black box with no derivative | surface interpolation (below) |
| `tetfill` | `tetfill` | TetGen alone, surface in / volume out | a discrete algorithm with no derivative | exact transpose of a gather |
| `thermal_jaxfem` | `thermal_solver` | jax-fem Poisson solve | AD strategy: JAX cannot trace PETSc assembly | implicit adjoint, bit-identical to in-process |
| `elastic_jaxfem` | `elastic_solver` | jax-fem linear elasticity + von Mises | same | same |
| `elastic_calculix` | `elastic_solver` | CalculiX 2.23 Fortran, over a subprocess | language, licence (GPL-2 isolated), AD strategy | native `*SENSITIVITY` adjoint plus a correction for a Jacobian-variation term missing from ccx 2.23, within 2e-4 of finite differences |
| `tet_gmsh` | `tet_mesher` | Gmsh (HXT, order 2) on a solid | licence (GPL-2-or-later isolated), a discrete topology decision | pass-through on `node_positions` |
| `flow_brinkman` | `flow_solver` | the [lattice-Boltzmann flow solver](flow.qmd), pure JAX | none | its own `custom_vjp`, bit-identical in-process and served |

Two plugins share `elastic_solver`; `[defaults]` in `plugins.toml` decides
which one answers. CalculiX cannot be traced, linked or relicensed, so the
plugin boundary composes its native adjoint with JAX autodiff while it stays a
subprocess. The
[simulator ecosystem survey](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/research/simulator-ecosystem.md)
ranks 31 further solvers (jwave, JAX-Fluids, MJX, …) that fit the same slots.
The solver ABI and the ccx correction are in
[FEM integration](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/research/fem-integration.md).

## Mesher boundaries {#the-two-mesher-boundaries}

**`tetfill`** receives an extracted surface (`points`, `triangles`) and never
sees the field. TetGen runs in PLC mode with `-Y`, which keeps input vertices
verbatim as the leading output nodes, so the VJP is the transpose of a gather
read off the `parents` table. Dual contouring stays upstream in JAX against the
true SDF, so creases stay sharp. TET4 and TET10.

**`mesher`** takes a field sampled on a lattice and does extraction, Newton
projection and TetGen or voxelization inside. Its VJP never looks in: a
boundary vertex `v` lies on the zero set of the trilinearly interpolated
samples, so the implicit function theorem gives

$$\frac{\partial v}{\partial f_i} = -\,w_i(v)\,\frac{\nabla f}{|\nabla f|^2}$$

The interpolation weights at the frozen vertices are the VJP rows, so any
mesher (TetGen, fTetWild, Gmsh) can sit behind it, including one that does not
preserve input vertices. The boundary is pinned to the interpolant's zero set,
which smears sharp features, and only the normal component of boundary motion
is carried. TET4, HEX8 and TET10.

Use `tetfill` wherever TetGen's vertex-preserving mode applies, and `mesher`
for a black-box mesher or HEX8. The validation matrix is in
[tet vs hex](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/research/tet-vs-hex.md).

### `tet_gmsh` {#tet_gmsh}

`tet_gmsh` takes a solid (`geometry` plus `geometry_format`) and returns a
TET10 mesh sized by the part. The default input is the dual-contour surface as
an STL, which Gmsh's `classifySurfaces` + `createGeometry` split into one
reparametrised surface per smooth region: on a plate with a bore, three
thousand facets in and a dozen surfaces out. `geometry_format="step"` meshes a
STEP file with the same contract; it benefits from a finer input than the
faceted STEP cadjoint writes.

Patch ownership is decided on the caller's side by
`cadjoint.fem.gmsh.assign_ownership`: for every Gmsh surface entity, `|f_p|` is
evaluated on its nodes for every patch of the scene, and a patch whose worst
node clears the bar owns the surface. Arity follows from the entity: one field
on a surface, two on a curve, three at a corner. An STL's nodes lie on facets,
so a curved face sags by `h²/8r` (3.5e-3 on a 0.25 bore at a 0.083 cell, above
a 2.7e-3 bar). Every boundary node is therefore Newton-projected with
`project_points` first, and the projected position is kept only where it
confirms more patches. On the plate at `target_size=0.16` this moves 264 of
1 700 boundary nodes and removes all 265 spurious blend nodes; the worst radius
ratio stays 0.293. The projection fixes ownership, not position: bore nodes
land within 2.4e-3 of `r = 0.25`.

Topology is frozen at discovery, so the VJP with respect to `node_positions`
is a pass-through. Moving nodes with the design is the `node_map` kind's job.

Gmsh is GPL-2.0-or-later and cadjoint is Apache-2.0, so nothing under
`cadjoint/` imports Gmsh at module scope. The supported route is the
`cadjoint_tet_gmsh` image, where the licence boundary is a process boundary;
`pip install 'cadjoint[gmsh]'` links it into your process instead (the `fem`
extra also pulls it in, because jax-fem imports it). In a scene,
`SimMesh(method="tet10", mesher="gmsh")` routes through this slot and returns
the same `TetMesh` node layout as TetGen; see
[meshing](meshing.qmd#the-gmsh-route).

## Transports {#one-contract-two-transports}

Only the `PluginSpec` knows where a plugin runs. `transport` is a closed set,
normalised to `PluginTransport`; any other value is rejected.

| Transport | Call | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `local` | `Tesseract.from_tesseract_api(api_path)` | default; same process, no Docker, no serialization |
| `container` | `Tesseract.from_image(image)` then `serve()` | a built image, torn down when the plugin closes |
| `remote` | `Tesseract.from_url(url)` | anything already serving: `tesseract serve`, `tesseract-runtime serve`, a Kubernetes Service |
| `python` | `getattr(import_module(module), attribute)` for `object = "module:attribute"` | a component called inside a trace or once per compile; needs no tesseract-core |

A Tesseract suits a coarse component called once per optimizer step: a served
round trip costs ~10 ms (see [Limitations](#limitations)). It does not suit a
component inside a trace. An in-process Tesseract round trip costs ~0.14 s,
while a two-field Newton projection of 300 points is 0.4 ms, a curve-tracer
step is sub-millisecond, and a `vmap` cannot contain a round trip at all. A
Tesseract also lacks the `jvp` and batching semantics of the component's own
`custom_vjp`. Such a component declares a typed `Protocol` in
`cadjoint.plugins.contracts` (frozen-dataclass payloads) and the registry binds
it to either transport; its Tesseract form is a thin `tesseract_api.py` over
the same object, which is how `tet_gmsh` is written.

`options` in a spec is forwarded unchanged to the constructor (`timeout`,
`environment`, `volumes`, `num_workers`, `gpus`, …).

### Runtime scratch directory

Every Tesseract endpoint call opens a `run_<uuid>/logs/` directory under the
runtime's output path, which defaults to the working directory. The `local`
transport passes `output_path=cadjoint.plugins.runtime_scratch()`: one
directory per process under `~/.cache/cadjoint/tesseract-runs` (override with
`$CADJOINT_TESSERACT_RUNS`), removed at exit. A server started by hand needs
`TESSERACT_OUTPUT_PATH`:

```bash
TESSERACT_API_PATH=cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/mesher/tesseract_api.py \
TESSERACT_OUTPUT_PATH="$HOME/.cache/cadjoint/tesseract-runs" \
TESSERACT_NAME=cadjoint_mesher TESSERACT_VERSION=0.1.0 \
tesseract-runtime serve --port 8000
```

The run logs are always written; they can only be redirected.

## Pluggable kinds {#pluggable-kinds}

[]{#the-five-in-process-kinds}

Five kinds are slots for a component that re-solves a surface against the
scene's patch fields with a derivative: a STEP whose bore is one cylinder, a
traced rather than sampled edge curve, a Gmsh mesh whose nodes follow the
design. Nothing in this repository fills them. Such a component ships
separately as ordinary `cadjoint.plugins` entry points, and cadjoint calls
whatever the registry returns through the Protocol.

| Kind | Protocol | In | Out |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node_map` | `NodeMap.positions` | scene, parameters, an `OwnedNodes` record | `(P, 3)` positions, **differentiable** in the parameters |
| `feature_edges` | `FeatureEdges.feature_edges` | scene, grid | an `EdgeSet` of polylines (NumPy, no derivative) |
| `brep` | `BRepExtractor.extract` | scene, grid | the derived B-rep, opaque, never leaves the process |
| `step_export` | `StepExporter.step_export` | scene, grid, path | a file, and the writer's report |
| `drag` | `Drag.drag` | scene, B-rep, handle, target | a `DragOutcome` |

`node_map` runs inside the jitted objective `Optimization` builds, so its
`custom_vjp` must be a primitive of the caller's program; this is why the
`python` transport exists. Its input, `OwnedNodes`, holds per node a seed
position, the owning patch indices, the arity, the Gmsh entity dimension, the
midside block and the ownership bar.

`CONTRACT_VERSION` in `cadjoint.plugins.contracts` bumps whenever a Protocol
or payload changes shape; a component with a stale `contract_version` is
refused with a sentence. One provider exists as a separate distribution;
installing it registers it through entry points, and a component of your own
registered the same way is treated identically.

`cadjoint.tier` reports whether a kind is filled:

```python
from cadjoint import tier

tier.status().flags()      # {'node_map': False, 'feature_edges': False, ...}
tier.available("brep")     # False
tier.component("step_export")            # None: the caller degrades
tier.require("node_map")                 # raises TierUnavailable(<one sentence>)
tier.report()                            # versions + status, for a bug report
```

With the kinds unfilled, cadjoint compiles, meshes with TetGen or Gmsh,
solves, inspects, exports VTK and faceted STEP, and draws feature edges from
the lattice classifier. One thing is refused: a Gmsh-meshed study cannot be
optimized, because its mesh is frozen geometry, and `Optimization` refuses it at
declaration rather than returning a wrong gradient. `mesher="tetgen"`, the
default, is differentiable either way. The compile payload carries a `tier` field and
`GET /api/capabilities` returns `tier.status()`, so the viewer labels which
layer it draws.

## Configuration

The config file is `$CADJOINT_PLUGINS` (a file, or a directory holding
`plugins.toml`), else `~/.config/cadjoint/plugins.toml`. A
`[plugins.<name>]` table for an existing name replaces its spec; a new name
adds a plugin. `${VAR}` expands from the environment, and an unset variable is
an error.

```toml
[defaults]
elastic_solver = "elastic_calculix"
feature_edges = "my_edges"

[plugins.thermal_jaxfem]
kind = "thermal_solver"
transport = "remote"
url = "http://thermal.cadjoint.svc.cluster.local:8000"
schema_hash = "sha256:251b6bd67db3f..."   # see Probing
options = { timeout = 600.0 }

[plugins.elastic_calculix]
kind = "elastic_solver"
transport = "container"
image = "cadjoint_elastic_calculix:latest"
options = { environment = { CADJOINT_CCX = "/python-env/bin/ccx" } }

[plugins.acoustics]
kind = "acoustic_solver"
transport = "remote"
url = "http://${ACOUSTICS_HOST}:8000"

[plugins.my_edges]
kind      = "feature_edges"
transport = "python"
object    = "my_package.edges:COMPONENT"
```

A distribution registers plugins without a config file through the
`cadjoint.plugins` entry point group; a value is a `PluginSpec`, a dict, or a
callable returning one:

```toml
# in the third party's pyproject.toml
[project.entry-points."cadjoint.plugins"]
acoustics = "my_package.plugins:SPEC"
node_map  = "my_package.plugins:NODE_MAP"   # PluginSpec(transport="python", object=...)
```

tesseract-core 1.11's `Tesseract.from_url` takes no header or credential
argument, and cadjoint does not modify its HTTP session. Put authentication in
front of the Service (an ingress, a sidecar, a service mesh) or use
`kubectl port-forward`.

## Writing a plugin

A plugin is a Tesseract package plus a spec. The package is a directory with
`tesseract_api.py`, `tesseract_config.yaml` and a requirements or environment
file; see `cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/*`, and
`tests/fem/test_tesseract_packaging.py` for what the SDK validates.
`tesseract_api.py` declares the schema cadjoint reads back:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from tesseract_core.runtime import Array, Differentiable, Float64, Int32

class InputSchema(BaseModel):
    points: Differentiable[Array[(None, 3), Float64]]
    cells: Array[(None, None), Int32]
    conductivity: Differentiable[Array[(), Float64]]

class OutputSchema(BaseModel):
    temperature: Differentiable[Array[(None,), Float64]]

def apply(inputs: InputSchema) -> OutputSchema: ...
def abstract_eval(abstract_inputs): ...
def vector_jacobian_product(inputs, vjp_inputs, vjp_outputs, cotangent_vector): ...
```

Register it through `plugins.toml`, an entry point, or for one process:

```python
from cadjoint.plugins import PluginSpec, register_plugin

register_plugin(
    PluginSpec(
        name="my_thermal",
        kind="thermal_solver",
        transport="local",
        api_path="my_package/thermal/tesseract_api.py",
    ),
    default=True,
)
```

To fill a cadjoint kind, the package must declare every input the frozen chain
sends for that kind and the output it reads; the chain checks this before
tracing and names any missing field. `elastic_calculix` declares no
`body_force`, so it cannot serve `elastic_solver` for the frozen chains but
remains a backend for direct solves.

## Building and serving

```bash
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/mesher           # ~1 min
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/elastic_calculix # ~1.5 min
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/thermal_jaxfem   # ~3 min
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/elastic_jaxfem   # ~3 min
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/tet_gmsh
tesseract build cadjoint/fem/tesseracts/flow_brinkman    # pure JAX, pip provider
```

| Image | Requirements provider | Payload | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cadjoint_mesher` | pip | cadjoint + TetGen + SciPy on CPython 3.12 | 1.36 GB |
| `cadjoint_elastic_calculix` | conda | ccx 2.23 from conda-forge at `/python-env/bin/ccx`, pinned via `CADJOINT_CCX` | 2.57 GB |
| `cadjoint_thermal_jaxfem` | conda | jax-fem stack: PETSc/petsc4py 3.25.5, gmsh, fenics-basix, meshio | 5.51 GB |
| `cadjoint_elastic_jaxfem` | conda | same | 5.51 GB |

The jax-fem stack is not pip-installable on Linux (petsc4py has no PyPI wheels,
gmsh has manylinux wheels for x86-64 only), and ccx is a Fortran binary. cadjoint
is a local path dependency, which `tesseract build` stages into the build
context.

`tesseract serve <image>` is what a Kubernetes Deployment should run; point a
`remote` spec at the Service in front of it. `tesseract serve a b c` serves
several Tesseracts together. Locally, `tesseract-runtime serve --port <n>`
with `TESSERACT_API_PATH` set serves a package directly, as `tests/plugins/`
does.

### Prebuilt images {#prebuilt-images}

Every push to `main` publishes the images to GHCR
(`.github/workflows/tesseract-images.yml`). A `container` spec that names one
pulls it on first use (cadjoint pulls before `Tesseract.from_image`, which does
not):

```toml
[plugins.thermal_jaxfem]
kind = "thermal_solver"
transport = "container"
image = "ghcr.io/andrinr/cadjoint_thermal_jaxfem:latest"
```

| Tag | Moves when |
|---|---|
| `:latest` | every publish from `main` |
| `:<version>` | the `version` in `tesseract_config.yaml`, what `probe()` reports |
| `:sha-<commit>` | never; pin this for a reproducible run |

Images are multi-arch (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) except `cadjoint_tet_gmsh`,
which is amd64 only because gmsh publishes no linux/aarch64 wheels; Docker on
Apple Silicon runs it under emulation. Each architecture is built on a native
runner and joined into one tag: the Dockerfile tesseract-core generates pins
its build stage to `$BUILDPLATFORM`, so a cross-building `buildx --platform`
would copy a host-architecture environment into the arm64 image.

## Probing

`Plugin.probe()` calls the runtime's `/health`, reads the advertised version,
and hashes the published schema:

```python
from cadjoint.plugins import get_plugin

probe = get_plugin("thermal_jaxfem").probe()
# PluginProbe(name='thermal_jaxfem', kind='thermal_solver', transport='local',
#             status='ok', version='0.1.0', schema_hash='sha256:251b6b…', …)
```

With `schema_hash` in the spec, a redeployed component whose interface changed
is rejected before a run. The hash covers field names, shapes, dtypes,
`Differentiable` flags and requiredness, and is identical across the `local`
and `remote` forms of a package. It excludes the endpoint list, because an
in-process runtime serves a `test` endpoint a served one does not.
`TESSERACT_NAME` / `TESSERACT_VERSION` make a hand-started server advertise a
version.

## Gradient paths and backends

`gradient_path` on an [`Optimization`](optimization.qmd) selects which frozen
chain runs:

| `gradient_path` | Plugin kinds it resolves |
|---|---|
| `"direct"` (default) | none: in-process JAX and jax-fem |
| `"tesseract"` (alias `"plugins"`) | `mesher` → `thermal_solver`/`elastic_solver` |
| `"tesseract-dc"` (alias `"plugins-dc"`) | `tetfill` → `thermal_solver`/`elastic_solver` |

`SolverBackend` (`backend="jaxfem" | "tesseract" | "calculix"`) resolves the
same way: `"tesseract"` takes the `thermal_solver` / `elastic_solver` kinds,
and `"calculix"` names the `elastic_calculix` plugin.

## Limitations

- **Remote overhead.** Measured 2026-09-02 on macOS/arm64 with the `mesher`
  package at 1285 nodes / 912 cells (74 KB in, 31 KB out), twelve
  `jax.value_and_grad` steps, `tesseract-runtime serve` on loopback:

  | | In-process | Served over HTTP |
  |---|---|---|
  | 12 steps | 6.57 s / 7.05 s | 6.69 s / 7.14 s |
  | per step | 548 ms / 587 ms | 558 ms / 595 ms |
  | objective | 342.8520334386417 → 342.8408938752647 | identical, all 13 digits |

  The wire adds 1.3–1.8%. That is the best case: no scheduler, TLS or
  queueing. A cluster adds network latency to every apply and VJP, twice per
  optimizer step per stage. On larger meshes the relative overhead falls,
  because the payload grows linearly and the solve faster.
- **No zero-size arrays over HTTP.** tesseract-core 1.11 validates polymorphic
  dimensions as `PositiveInt`. The mesher's discovery mode (empty `point_ids`
  and `cell_template`) must run in-process; pass the topology it returns to
  the served instance. The frozen chains send `cell_conductivity` /
  `cell_youngs` / `body_force` as empty arrays on the single-material path, so
  a `thermal_solver` or `elastic_solver` cannot run `remote` in a chain run;
  the mesher stage and direct solves can.
- **TetGen topology is platform-dependent.** The same field meshes to 182
  points on macOS/arm64 and 185 in the Linux container, so a frozen TET4/TET10
  topology does not transfer between host and container. HEX8 is
  deterministic across both.
